title: Artifact viewer inline text preview: a file extension must be added to both the server text-extension list and the client TEXT_EXTENSIONS set
answers: Jupyter notebook (.ipynb) artifact downloads instead of previewing inline in the artifact viewer
How do I make a new text-like file type show inline in the run artifact viewer?
Where is the list of artifact extensions treated as text for preview handled?
Why does fixing the served Content-Type on the server not make the artifact preview appear in the UI?
body:
Path: Artifact viewer for run/model artifacts. The server decides the served Content-Type from file extension via mlflow/utils/mime_type_utils.py:get_text_extensions, and the React page ShowArtifactPage.tsx chooses inline text preview versus download from the extension using TEXT_EXTENSIONS in mlflow/server/js/src/common/utils/FileUtils.ts.
Rule: When a text-like extension should preview inline, add it to both get_text_extensions() (server, yields text/plain) and TEXT_EXTENSIONS (client dispatch). The client keys preview on the extension, not on the response Content-Type, so a server-only change leaves the file downloaded.
Symptom: A .ipynb notebook artifact was served as application/octet-stream and the viewer prompted a download instead of showing the contents inline.
Constraints: Covers plain-text formats rendered as raw text only. Markdown, HTML and image types use separate sets (MARKDOWN_EXTENSIONS, HTML_EXTENSIONS) and are not affected by TEXT_EXTENSIONS. The notebook is shown as raw JSON text, not rendered as a notebook. Storage and download behaviour are unchanged.
applies: Any change that makes a new file extension previewable in the MLflow artifact viewer (server mime mapping plus the frontend preview set).
says: Jupyter notebook files download automatically instead of displaying inside the artifact viewer pane.
Clicking a notebook artifact prompts a browser download rather than showing an inline preview.
Preview text-based files directly on screen in the run artifact tab instead of downloading.
Make Jupyter notebooks viewable as raw text inside the web interface artifact viewer.
Adding server MIME types for text artifacts still forces browser downloads in the web UI.
search: To enable inline text preview for a new file extension in the artifact viewer, the extension must be added to both `mlflow/utils/mime_type_utils.py:get_text_extensions` on the server and `mlflow/server/js/src/common/utils/FileUtils.ts:TEXT_EXTENSIONS` on the frontend. `ShowArtifactPage.tsx` decides whether to render inline text or prompt a download based on the extension via the frontend set rather than the server response Content-Type header. This applies only to plain-text formats rendered as raw text, whereas markdown, HTML, and images use separate sets and notebook rendering or artifact storage remains unchanged.
